title: user-affinity-routing-micro-prd-scratchpad
content:
Quick brain dump: idea to add a lightweight user-affinity routing layer to increase KV/prefix cache hits across requests for the same logical user or session, without heavy session storage.

Context / why:
- We see regression in per-request latency on small prompt workloads due to cold KV cache misses; Dedicated customers reported higher p99 when requests are spread across hosts.
- Existing solutions: sticky sessions (heavy), per-connection affinity (not feasible for serverless-hosted), session-store (we have a PRD for session-store but that is larger scope).
- Goal: improve latency & token-cost by increasing cache hit probability using routing heuristics and short-lived affinity tokens.

High-level concept:
- Issue (from client) includes optional affinity token in header (x-rw-affinity) or we generate an affinity token at routing time and return it in response headers.
- Routing layer maps affinity token -> preferred serving node/pool variant for N minutes (configurable TTL 30s-10min). Node chosen to maximize KV cache reuse (same model variant, same host, same quantization profile).
- Affinity is best-effort: if target node is unavailable, fall back to normal routing; no hard lock.
- Affinity tokens are opaque to customers; can be rotated. Tokens carry no PII.

User stories:
- As a product app, I want repeated short-turn interactions to hit the same serving node to reduce latency.
- As infra, I want to keep affinity state tiny and ephemeral so we don't require durable session DB.
- As security/sysadmin, I need the token to be non-identifying and to expire quickly.

Design sketch / pieces:
1) Token issuance: router returns Set-Affinity header on requests that are good candidates (long-running KV benefit or multi-turn). Also clients can pass affinity by header when known.
2) Local affinity table: per-router limited map (LRU) affinityKey -> (node, expiry). Keep size low (10k entries per router) and TTL short.
3) Affinity scoring function: reuseScore = f(lastSeen, modelVariantMatch, regionMatch, recentCacheHitRate). Prefer nodes with best expected cache hit.
4) Fallbacks: if node unreachable or overloaded, route normally and optionally invalidate affinity entry.
5) Opt-out: some customers can disable via tenant flag; also do not attach affinity for requests flagged with sensitive content (privacy concerns).

Metrics we care about:
- delta p50/p95/p99 latency for repeat requests with affinity vs baseline
- KV cache hit rate uplift
- percentage of requests carrying affinity token
- affinity table hit ratio + churn
- failed affinity fallbacks
- cost delta (tokens saved)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Router can issue and honor affinity tokens with TTL default 2 min.
- Affinity table implementation with metrics and <1% overhead on router CPU.
- End-to-end experiment on internal traffic shows >=8% p95 improvement on targeted workloads and >=15% KV cache hit increase.
- Feature can be toggled per-tenant and turned off globally.

Rollout plan (quick experiment):
- Phase 0: unit + integration tests (router/local map), dry-run telemetry (no actual routing change) to collect signals (2 weeks).
- Phase 1: internal alpha traffic + dev teams (5% traffic) — measure metrics (2 weeks).
- Phase 2: small set of Dedicated customers opt-in (via feature flag) (3 weeks).
- Phase 3: broader opt-in + auto-enablement for small prompt workloads if net benefit positive.

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: ensure tokens never include user id or tenant id. If customer encrypts content, token still safe. Confirm legal review for EU (GDPR) — pinged legal (INF-PRIV-ops).
- Multi-region: affinity might prefer local node; but cross-region failover needs clear TTL/invalidation.
- Consistency vs freshness: long affinity TTL increases cache reuse but reduces ability to rebalance; choose sensible defaults.
- Impact on autoscaling decisions: if many tokens stick to a few nodes, hotspots may form. Need circuit-breaker + rebalance heuristics.

Engineering notes / TODOs:
- Prototype in routing service (repo routing) as middleware; reuse existing local in-memory maps.
- Add telemetry events: AFFINITY_ISSUED, AFFINITY_USED, AFFINITY_MISS, AFFINITY_FALLBACK.
- Add admin endpoints to inspect affinity table per-router for debugging (read-only, internal only).
- Add per-tenant opt-out flag stored in config service.

Related tickets / quick links:
- INF-2741 (initial spike) — linked above
- routing PR #198 — prototype code
- slack thread: #eng-platform "affinity routing idea" (C02ABC123)

Notes to self (short):
- Keep semantics simple. MVP should not require durable session store.
- Make sure we can revoke tokens quickly (invalidate on config change).
- Demo: show p95 reduction on internal chatbot flow where user sends 3 quick prompts within 90s.

Next actions (this week):
- Sync with Kai (kernel selection impacts) and Noah (SRE concerns) — schedule 30m sync.
- Draft RFC for team review (put in product repo).
- Add telemetry proto (inf.metrics) and wire to datadog dashboards.

-- end of scratchpad --
